title: Bernstein–Vazirani
summary: Recover a whole secret string in one query.
mission: Find the 4-bit secret string s with a single call to oracle(qc): at the end, the input register (qubits 0 to 3) must be in the state |s⟩. Convention: qubit 0 corresponds to the last character of s, that is, s = s3 s2 s1 s0 and the state label is |q3 q2 q1 q0⟩.

prediction.question: Can a randomized classical algorithm that accepts a 1% error find a 4-bit secret string with fewer than 4 queries?
prediction.explanation: Each query returns a single bit, so with fewer than 4 queries more than one string is consistent with the answers, and a guess is right with probability at most 1/2: far from 99%. Randomness does not help here, while the quantum algorithm uses one query, for any length of s.

hints: The circuit is the same as Deutsch-Jozsa, now with 4 input qubits and the auxiliary on qubit 4.
Auxiliary in |−⟩ with qc.x(4) and qc.h(4); Hadamard on qubits 0 to 3 before and after the oracle.
Use a loop for qubit in range(4): qc.h(qubit). It appears twice, around oracle(qc).
